name: Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment (Male Patients)
description: Improvement by treatment for the 25 male patients in the arthritis trial — a borderline association (p ≈ 0.09). IMS Ch. 18 (chi-square).
studyDescription: The male patients (n = 25) from a double-blind clinical trial of an active treatment versus placebo for rheumatoid arthritis. Each patient was randomly assigned to the treatment or the placebo group, and their improvement was later rated as None, Some, or Marked. Because the sample is small (some expected cell counts are below 5), a randomization test is more appropriate here than the chi-square approximation.

variableDescriptions.treatment: Whether the patient received the active treatment or a placebo (assigned at random).
variableDescriptions.improved: The degree of improvement in the patient’s rheumatoid arthritis, rated None, Some, or Marked.

sourceDetail: Koch & Edwards (1988), via the R vcd package (vcd::Arthritis), male subset. χ² = 4.91, df = 2, p = 0.086.

inferenceContexts.parameter: there is an association between treatment and improvement among the male arthritis patients
inferenceContexts.claim: the active treatment changes the distribution of improvement outcomes compared with placebo (male patients)
